title: Confluence
subtitle: From the silent kingdom of the dead, a sliver of light escapes.

trails.title: Witness Report
trails.description: An unremarkable witness report. All rumors, whispers, and tales—every passerby keeps a few in their pockets.

content.text: A boatman on the Seine says he saw unusual blue flames near the riverbank one night. They disappeared when he got closer. He insists he's never seen will-o'-the-wisps in all his twenty years on the river.

items.text: Confluence
The Catacombs
Bricks and soil several stories high shut out the sunlight above. Footsteps making dull echoes through the underground passage.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: This should be about where the restricted area begins.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Though I doubt the police have the luxury of worrying about our trespassing.
The carvings inside the lampshade emit a steady faint light, bathing the tunnel in a soft glow.
Dust long settled on the rough stone floor rises into the air, as if the space were rushing up to meet its rare visitors.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I've always wanted to explore the catacombs; it's almost eerie to think they've been lying beneath our feet for centuries.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: And it only got spookier once they started stuffing the dead away down here. A vast labyrinth lined with skeletons ...

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But, despite the spookiness, I still feel it has a special charm—secret passages used by revolutionaries and soldiers, surviving in their own way against the march of progress.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The catacombs have a rich history indeed. Yet only a small portion of it remains open to the public.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: It is a place dear to the spirit of the city, yet one that is hidden away.
Her companion finishes the sentence Adèle hadn't.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Oh, pardon. I'm treating you like one of my clients. I'm sure you don't need a guide to tell you these things.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Besides, we aren't here for sightseeing.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I need to find Célia and get her to safety as soon as possible.
They come to a confluence of paths. Adèle's heart tugs as her purpose meets yet another frustration.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But these tunnels stretch out almost three hundred kilometers in all directions. We can't go looking for a needle in a haystack.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Madame, your divination revealed Célia's whereabouts before. Could you perhaps try it again?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The fates of many commingle here. To trace her would be to catch a single stream from a flowing river.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: But it seems her stream is deeply entangled with your own. Perhaps, by observing yours, I may discern her presence.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Your stream is quite unique. The familial curse you bear—it may be a gift in some strange way, setting you on a path unlike any other.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I've certainly never thought of it that way.
Though in saying that, she finds herself back in the Parlor of Crystals, weighing her attitude toward fate—her dismissal of it.
She shakes her head and sighs.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But you're saying you can track her, aren't you?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: It will not show me where she is, but I will gain some sense of where she has been.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Awesome. Better than searching blindly.
Beryl nods, her crystal pendulum emitting a dim light.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: To the left.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Okay, then we go left.
Fork in the Road, Catacombs
They turn another corner, and the next corridor ahead looks much the same as the last.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Wait! I should leave some sort of mark.
Adèle picks up a stone and scratches yet another arrow on the wall.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Umm, we've been walking for a while now, but we still haven't found anything. Forgive me, madame, but are you sure your divination—

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Shh.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Look. The fruits of your search.
Following Beryl's gaze, she catches a silhouette flicker at the far end.
She crouches, raising her hand slightly, ready to strike with her flames if needed.
Adèle watches guardedly as the figure steps into the light.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Who's there? Oh, a fellow explorer? What luck! You see, my headlamp's gone out, and I've been separated from my students.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: I wonder if you might help me get to the surf—wait, you! Are you not that same young lady from yesterday?

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: And you, Madame Beryl Bouanich?

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: What on earth are you two doing here?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You know each other?
Adèle looks back at Beryl, but her suspicion washes up against her calm composure.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I have attended a number of Professor Roseau's lectures. His ideas are most intriguing.
Beryl's introduction is cut notably short. But it hints all the more at how wide her influence reaches.
But this man himself does not earn any trust for being an acquaintance's acquaintance.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Was Célia with you, Professor? I've been looking for her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: It's serious. I tried calling the campus, but no one answered.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Célia? She was supposed to join us today, yes, but I'm afraid I haven't seen her. Most unlike her to do such a thing, but perhaps she had a change of plans.
Adèle studies the man's bewildered face. A thought crosses her mind.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Forgive me.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Huh?
Feufeu lunges for the professor's wrist, sending fire crawling up his fingers.
The flames flicker, fading quickly, leaving only a trace of warmth. The fire accepts him.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Ms. Tavernier! What are you doing?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No need to be alarmed; it's just my arcane skill. It's a relief to know you're as real as you appear.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But you have heard about the reappearance of the Beasts of Gévaudan, no? To say nothing of the Critters that surely nest down here ...

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Monsters wearing human skin could be lurking nearby. We can't be too cautious.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: I appreciate the warning.
He brushes away imaginary ashes from his sleeve and resumes the prior conversation.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Knowing Célia, it may very well be that she lost track of time organizing her research materials. Are you quite certain she's not at home?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: That does sound like her. But I went to her place. No one was there.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: In all likelihood, she's in some café with her nose buried in a book. But miss, why is it that you are so concerned with finding her?

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: It's as if you're certain she's in some kind of danger.
She cannot help but notice he's moved one hand behind his back—a guarded stance.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: She may well be. Madame Bouanich has had a premonition.
They go over a brief account of the prophecy, the nightmare, and the necklace that serves as proof.
When she finishes, the professor exhales softly, before bursting into laughter.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Madame Bouanich, forgive my bluntness, but you've been indulging this young lady far too much.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Scurrying about down here? What this young lady needs is a good rest.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: It is her will that brought us here.
He turns to Adèle, pity mingling with paternalism in a single toxic facade, as if she had only been some babbling child pointing at a monster beneath her bed.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Miss, I know you're a dear friend of Célia's and worried about her safety ...

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: But you mustn't let yourself become paranoid, especially with all of this hysteria spreading through the city as of late.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Are you saying I'm making things up? That this is just some kind of mania?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: It isn't! Absolutely not! How else could you explain the necklace!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: There may be many explanations—many indeed. Though I fear, in the worst case, that you've been under the spell of this mania for much longer than you realize.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Think, miss. This necklace you were given in this dream of yours ... Where did it go? Where is it now?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I-It was Félicienne. She—
Adèle hesitates mid-step.
Bringing up her vanishing employer would only make the situation worse.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I remember ... I saw it ...
She wrings her memory like a dry sponge.
At the end of the tomb's darkness, she spies the same fur that had haunted her dream.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Watch out!
The furry shadow screams and darts away, its cry louder than her gasp.
